narrative.overview:
Foundry keeps a B2B buyer and supplier workflow in one workspace: discover products, compare supplier specifications, send an inquiry, complete order details, confirm payment, and follow delivery. A persistent navigation rail keeps each role’s next task in reach while the main canvas changes between catalog, orders, listings, tracking, and account views.

The interface uses DM Sans, a quiet green action color, white task surfaces, and cool neutral framing. Green identifies the primary action and current navigation item; amber, blue, and green status treatments distinguish order states. Supplier-provided images are shown as supplied. When there is no image, a labeled neutral placeholder makes that absence clear.
keyCharacteristics: Role-aware navigation for buyers and suppliers.
Product cards that keep price, specifications, supplier, and inquiry action together.
Order progress shown as named steps, with actions appearing at the relevant state.
Personal delivery details shown in the authorized order context only.

rules.name: The Source-and-Status Rule
rules.body: Use the primary green for the current task and selected location. Use semantic status colors only to explain an order or system state; never use them as decoration.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Keep labels, forms, cards, and navigation in DM Sans. Use weight and size to establish hierarchy rather than introducing a display face.

rules.name: The Role-Rail Rule
rules.body: Keep buyer and supplier destinations in the left navigation; change the main content to the selected task without hiding role context.

rules.name: The Clear-Feedback Rule
rules.body: Use separate colors for success, information, and error notices. Expose errors with alert semantics and other feedback with status semantics.

dos: Do keep buyer and supplier actions role-specific and close to their related records.
Do show the current order state and name the next available step.
Do keep payment verification visibly ahead of packing and shipment actions.
Do use supplier-provided product images and honest labeled placeholders when an image is absent.
Do distinguish success, information, and error notices with separate colors and retain accessible message semantics.
donts: Don't imply that image recognition, live checkout, supplier verification, or tracking-provider integrations exist when they are not connected.
Don't show delivery addresses outside the buyer’s order or the assigned supplier’s order detail.
Don't use status colors as decoration or replace status labels with color alone.
